claim: A real controller SIGKILL closes the LinuxSupervisor input pipe; the actual packaged Java supervisor aborts, terminates/reaps its owned workload and removes its inner cgroup and gate state on Linux x86-64 and ARM64.

documentation_class_equivalence.reason: Four one-line Javadoc block-return tags changed to inline-return tags, preserving source line positions. No runtime check repeated for this documentation-only repair.

fixture.role: Diagnostic-only controller JVM exercises the production public operation from its actual named module. The separate Python observer kills that controller, adopts/reaps its supervisor through Linux subreaper semantics, verifies native effects and owns test cleanup. No production code is replaced.

local_verification.fixture_compilation: passed against the final tooling JAR and pinned module dependencies
local_verification.reason: Production source and compiled behavior are unchanged; only this previously unaccepted lifecycle boundary is exercised.

acceptance: Before controller death, a prepared gate or released detached descendant remains live and no workload result exists.
The actual controller process is SIGKILLed and reaped with exit -9, closing the retained supervisor input pipe without invoking controller close().
The supervisor reports controller-input EOF (-1), terminates and reaps the workload, removes its inner cgroup and gate scratch, and exits 1.
An independent observer adopts and reaps that supervisor; no child process remains and no result.xml is published.
The outer controller-owned cgroup is empty and retained attempt files remain available for recovery; the observer removes the empty test groups and later the client removes owned storage.
Both architectures pass both gated and released cases using the same production JAR, Java fixture and Python observer.
Both persistent Upterm clients verify workspace access before testing and remain through retries/collection. SSH exits zero; all hosted posts pass, with only the intentional exit-17 step failing.

workflow_failures.outcome: The original single-run selector rejected parallel dispatches as ambiguous.
workflow_failures.recovery: A target-job-name filter selects the already-dispatched x64 run; resume acquires its existing artifact and connects without another dispatch. The original launcher and its failure record are retained in the x64 client archive.

workflow_failures.cause: Unprivileged tar cannot read root-owned private supervisor attempt directories.
workflow_failures.recovery: Keep the native pass and original transcript; retry only tar under sudo on each same retained worker. Corrected collection exits zero; no native test is repeated.

telemetry_readiness.status: unavailable in fresh descendants without controller configuration
telemetry_readiness.claim: Both current runner service cgroups advertise the memory controller but have empty subtree_control. A fresh owned parent and child expose none of the four probed memory files; unavailable counters are not reported as zero.
telemetry_readiness.mutation: Only fresh owned empty cgroup directories are created and removed. No controller is enabled and no process is migrated.
telemetry_readiness.next: Select a checked whole-owned-tree memory observation that preserves inherited limits. Safe delegation or checked per-process RSS still needs proof; do not move work outside ancestor limits to obtain counters.

limitations: This accepts workload shutdown after controller death, not automatic recovery/removal of the dead controller-owned outer cgroup and attempt storage. Production workflow crash cleanup remains open.
The observer uses Python only for diagnostics. Production scheduling and ownership remain Java/JDK27.
The tested JAR predates four documentation-only source corrections; the prior committed class-equivalence evidence proves all 75 final class files byte-identical.
No complete scheduler loop, memory admission/effects, actual allocation blocking, other-platform composition or Cargo/Bazel integration is accepted by these cases.
Readonly TMOUT=1800 is configured before tests; idle expiration is not tested.
replay: Retrieve the prior supervisor evidence at commit 77d795e82047ae2f441d8cd1a6f0fc7194465e69. Decode this evidence remote archive for ControllerDeathFixture.java, controller-death.py, resolve.py and original receipts. Through an authenticated retained native Linux runner, run resolve.py in an exclusive owned directory to recover the exact tested JAR and pinned architecture-specific JDK. Run controller-death.py as root. Collect root-owned attempt evidence with sudo tar; complete finish-smoke.cjs if using runner-debug-smoke, remove only the owned directory, exit/reap SSH and verify hosted posts. The native observer creates and removes its exclusive cgroup parent and records the distinction between supervisor cleanup and observer recovery.
